subject: Re: Pricing stability & MFN/CPI guardrails — VectorScale commitment discussion
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@vectorscale.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@vectorscale.com
Date: 2026-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing stability / MFN / CPI cap for committed usage

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising for our realtime assistants. Procurement has asked me to confirm a couple of commercial items before we move to an LOI:

- VectorScale is planning a 12M commit for hosted tokens (~6B tokens/month average). We need a firm 12-month price lock on per-token rates for that committed tier.
- We also require an MFN on per-token price versus any public or announced committed pricing for comparable customers in the same geography and scale.
- Because our budget is indexed to inflation, we need CPI-based cap on annual price increases (max +2.5% year-over-year) after the initial 12-month lock.

Can Redwood confirm these guardrails? If so we can share the volume profile and a PO. If not, please propose alternatives.

Also attaching our internal MA plan for throughput assumptions.

Thanks,

Aisha Khan
Head of Cloud Procurement
VectorScale

Attachment: VectorScale_MA_plan.xlsx

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@vectorscale.com>
Date: 2026-04-11T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing stability / MFN / CPI cap for committed usage

Hi Aisha — great talking to you too. Appreciate the clear ask.

Short answers up-front: we can structure a commitment that provides a meaningful price reduction and multi-month stability, but we need to balance that with protection for Redwood and our other customers. Below is a proposed compromise that has worked for other large-ticket customers:

1) Commitment and price-lock
- 12-month committed volume: Redwood will lock per-token hosted rate for the committed tier for 12 months from contract execution. The lock applies to the quoted model family(s) only.

2) MFN scope
- We can accept a restricted MFN limited to materially comparable committed deals (publicly announced committed per-token rates or signed tuck-in agreements for customers with public scale >4B tokens/month). MFN will not apply to promotional or short-term campaigns, trials, or partner credits.

3) CPI / annual increases
- After the initial 12-month lock, we propose a cap of CPI + 1.0% (floor 0%), applied annually to the base per-token rate, with a maximum increase of 3.0% in any 12-month window. This is consistent with our standard commercial approach for large committed customers.

4) Downside / rollback triggers
- If we materially change model architecture (e.g., major new model with better price/perf) we would provide 60 days' notice and an option to migrate to the new family with a transitional credit; we expect this to be rare.

5) Legal & audit
- We can accept a limited audit right to verify usage/tiering once per 12 months, with mutually agreeable scope and redaction.

I attached a redlineable terms sheet (Redwood_Pricing_Termsheet_v2.pdf) with numeric examples for the committed tier and show rate breakpoints at 1B/3B/6B tokens. If this high-level approach looks reasonable, I'm happy to loop in Marissa and Rishi to finalize commercial terms and legal language.

Best,

— Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Termsheet_v2.pdf

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@vectorscale.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-12T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing stability / MFN / CPI cap for committed usage

Priyom — thanks for the quick reply and the redlineable sheet. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing: 

- VectorScale prefers the MFN to be broader: we'd like it to capture any committed published price for customers in the same sector and similar scale (not just "materially comparable"). The risk for us is that a later deal reduces per-token rates and we are locked in.
- On CPI, we are asking for a hard cap at +1.5% year-over-year. Our finance team cannot absorb CPI + 1.0% margins.
- For model migration we understand the notice requirement, but we need assurance that there will be no unilateral mid-term re-pricing of the committed model family that affects the locked rate.

If Redwood can accept MFN with an explicit carve-out for promotional trial pricing and keep the CPI cap to 1.5%, we can proceed to an LOI this week.

Aisha

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@vectorscale.com>
Date: 2026-04-13T10:41:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing stability / MFN / CPI cap for committed usage — need guidance

Marissa / Rishi — looping you in. VectorScale is asking for: (a) MFN broader than our typical language, (b) CPI cap at 1.5% (they asked 2.5 originally but now pushing 1.5%), and (c) explicit no mid-term re-pricing of committed model family.

My read: they are a strategic customer and the volume is meaningful, but broad MFN + tight CPI could constrain our pricing flexibility when we announce public enterprise discounts. Proposed negotiation posture:

- Accept a 12-month lock on the committed tier rates for the specified model family.
- Narrow MFN to committed, non-promotional public deals and require comparable scale (>=4B tokens/month). Offer a 30-day notification requirement if we publish lower committed pricing for new customers and a right for VectorScale to request parity within 60 days (parity by way of credit rather than retroactive invoice changes).
- Offer CPI cap at 1.75% fixed for years 2 and onward (instead of CPI+1.0).

Legal flags: MFN wording will need to be careful to avoid open-ended obligations. We should also consider adding a capped liability for pricing misapplication.

Can you confirm if leadership is comfortable conceding to 1.75% vs their 1.5% ask and approve the MFN as I described? If approved I will send a redline.

— Priyom

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-14T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing stability / MFN / CPI cap for committed usage — need guidance

Thanks for the summary, Priyom. I'm comfortable with the posture you proposed with one tweak: tighten the MFN notification window to 14 days (we'd notify quickly if we post a lower committed price) and insist any remediation is via prospective credits only (no retroactive refunds). Approve the CPI 1.75% compromise.

Rishi — legal should prepare a narrowly scoped MFN clause with: 1) definition of "committed public deals," 2) promotional carve-outs, 3) scale threshold >=4B tokens/month, 4) notification + 60-day request window, and 5) credit-based remediation with cap = 6 months of incremental discount difference.

Once legal has a redline I'll let Priyom share back with VectorScale.

Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@vectorscale.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-14T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Final commercial posture — VectorScale commitment (summary)

Aisha — following internal review we can move forward along these lines: 

- 12-month price lock on committed per-token rate for the specified model family.
- MFN: limited to publicly announced, committed deals at comparable scale (>=4B tokens/month). Promotional/trial pricing excluded. Redwood will notify VectorScale within 14 days if we publish a lower committed price; VectorScale may request parity within 60 days. Remediation will be provided as a prospective credit (no retroactive refunds) capped at 6 months of the discount difference.
- CPI: fixed annual cap of +1.75% for years after the initial 12-month lock.
- Model migration: 60 days' notice for material architecture changes and transitional credits as appropriate.
- Audit right: limited, once per 12 months.

If that aligns with VectorScale's needs I will share the redlined terms sheet and the LOI template for signatures.

Best,
Priyom
